prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Pleasanton CA for a checkup and cleaning?
answer_verbatim:
I can help — do you want a specific name(s) I can pick out for you, or would you like tips to find the best fit yourself? A couple quick questions so I recommend the right place:

- Do you have dental insurance (and which plan)?  
- Are you looking for an adult, child, or family dentist?  
- Any preferences (female/male dentist, language, near a particular ZIP code or landmark, weekend availability)?

If you want to decide on your own right now, here’s a fast checklist and practical steps to find the best dentist in Pleasanton for a routine checkup and cleaning:

What to use to find top options
- Google Maps and Yelp (look at number of reviews and overall rating).  
- Zocdoc for real-time appointment availability and patient feedback.  
- ADA “Find-a-Dentist” and the California Dental Board website to confirm licensing and any disciplinary history.  
- Your insurer’s provider directory (if you want in-network care).

What to look for in reviews and websites
- Consistently high ratings and recent reviews mentioning clean, on-time visits and gentle hygienists.  
- New-patient welcome info (first-visit forms, online booking).  
- Services offered: routine cleaning, digital X‑rays, periodontal care, same‑day emergency visits.  
- Office hours that fit your schedule and easy parking/location.

Questions to ask when you call
- Do you accept my insurance? What will be my out‑of‑pocket for a new‑patient exam and cleaning?  
- How long is the appointment for a cleaning? Who performs the cleaning (RDH hygienist or the dentist)?  
- Do you take X‑rays at first visit and what are the fees?  
- What COVID/sterilization protocols do you follow? Are you accepting new patients?

Typical cost expectations (Bay Area / Pleasanton)
- New patient exam: $50–$150 (varies).  
- Routine adult cleaning (prophy): roughly $75–$200 without insurance.  
- X‑rays: $25–$150 depending on type. Prices vary; check with office.

Red flags to avoid
- Pushy sales for expensive restorative work at first visit.  
- Poor or no sterilization information when asked.  
- Very old negative reviews about pain, rude staff, or billing issues.

If you want, tell me your zip code and whether you need in‑network providers, and I’ll provide a short list of highly rated Pleasanton dentists (or ask to run a web search now).
